## Summary

I fixed the bug in the minijinja template engine's include logic in `minijinja/src/vm/mod.rs`.

**Root cause:** The `State` maintains a `loaded_templates` set used for template-inheritance cycle detection (in `load_blocks`, which errors if a template name is `referenced more than once`). When `perform_include` renders an included template, it saved/restored `state.instructions`, `state.blocks`, `state.auto_escape`, and the closure — but **not** `state.loaded_templates`.

So when an included template used `{% extends %}`, the parent template's name was inserted into `loaded_templates` and never cleared. Including that same extended template again — e.g. once per iteration of a loop — hit the parent name still in the set on the second iteration and raised a false `cycle in template inheritance` error.

**Fix:** Each `include` starts an independent inheritance chain, so I `mem::take` the `loaded_templates` set (replacing it with a fresh empty set) for the duration of the include and restore the previous value afterward:

```rust
let old_loaded_templates = mem::take(&mut state.loaded_templates);
// ... eval the included template ...
state.loaded_templates = old_loaded_templates;
```

**Verification:** A reproduction (a `main` template looping three times over `{% include "child.html" %}`, where `child.html` extends `base.html`) now renders `[1][2][3]` correctly instead of erroring. The build is clean and no new test failures are introduced. I did not touch anything in `tests/`.

+use minijinja::Environment;
+
+fn main() {
+    let mut env = Environment::new();
+    env.add_template("base.html", "[{% block body %}{% endblock %}]").unwrap();
+    env.add_template("child.html", "{% extends \"base.html\" %}{% block body %}{{ item }}{% endblock %}").unwrap();

+    let out = tmpl.render(minijinja::context!(items => vec![1,2,3])).unwrap();
+    println!("OUTPUT: {}", out);
+    assert_eq!(out, "[1][2][3]");
+    println!("PASS");
+}

+    env.add_template("base.html", "[{% block body %}{% endblock %}]").unwrap();
+    env.add_template("child.html", "{% extends \"base.html\" %}{% block body %}{{ item }}{% endblock %}").unwrap();
+    env.add_template("main.html", "{% for item in items %}{% include \"child.html\" %}{% endfor %}").unwrap();
+    let tmpl = env.get_template("main.html").unwrap();
+    let out = tmpl.render(minijinja::context!(items => vec![1,2,3])).unwrap();
+    println!("OUTPUT: {}", out);
+    assert_eq!(out, "[1][2][3]");
+    println!("PASS");
+}
